newsitem.title: COMOROS: Comoros magistrates strike over interference.
newsitem.headline: Comoros magistrates strike over interference.

text.p: Magistrates on the Indian Ocean Comoro Islands have declared an indefinite strike to protest against government interference.
The strike was called after justice minister Ali Hassanaly asked the public prosecutor last week to remove from examining magistrates an investigation into the management of state companies.
"The magistrates are frequently put in a situation where it is impossible for them to dispense justice serenely," said a statement by magistrates on Saturday.

"The resumption of judiciary activities is conditioned on the appropriate solution the President of the Republic (Mohamed Taki), guarantor of the magistrates' independence, will bring to the actual situation," the statement said.
The Comoros, which have had 17 coups and attempted coups since independence from France in 1975, have this year been swept by a series of strikes by civil servants demanding salary arrears.
In March several people died and hundreds were arrested on Anjouan, the Comoros' second island, after clashes between stone-throwing villagers demanding secession and armed troops.
